evidence.title: What’s New In Python 3.10 — Python 3.15.0 documentation
evidence.text:
### distutils¶

The entire `distutils` package is deprecated, to be removed in Python 3.12. Its functionality for specifying package builds has already been completely replaced by third-party packages `setuptools` and `packaging`, and most other commonly used APIs are available elsewhere in the standard library (such as `platform`, `shutil`, `subprocess` or `sysconfig`). There are no plans to migrate any other functionality from `distutils`, and applications that are using other functions should plan to make private copies of the code. Refer to PEP 632 for discussion.

evidence.title: Idempotent requests | Stripe API Reference
evidence.text:
`500`

A client generates an idempotency key, which is a unique key that the server uses to recognize subsequent retries of the same request. How you create unique keys is up to you, but we suggest using V4 UUIDs, or another random string with enough entropy to avoid collisions. Idempotency keys are up to 255 characters long. Avoid using sensitive data (for example, email addresses or personal identifiers) as idempotency keys.

evidence.title: Idempotent requests | Stripe API Reference
evidence.text:
`IdempotencyKey`

For API v1, Stripe saves the status code and body of the first request made with a given idempotency key after endpoint execution begins. Retries with the same key return the saved response, including `500` errors. With API v2, retries don’t repeat successful operations. Stripe retries failed or partially failed work to completion when possible and returns an updated response. If a retry can’t succeed, Stripe returns an error explaining why.

evidence.text:
# Idempotent requests

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. When creating or updating an object, use an idempotency key. Then, if a connection error occurs, you can safely repeat the request without risk of creating a second object or performing the update twice.
